headline: TT&A, S&R, SAM and Agram act on Tata Motors taking control of Freight Tiger
sum: Tata Motors raised its stake in logistics-tech platform Freight Tiger to ~63% by buying out Lightspeed, Florintree and the founder for ₹95.66 cr.
detail: Tata Motors increased its stake in Freight Commerce Solutions (Freight Tiger) to ~63% by purchasing shares from three selling shareholders — Lightspeed India Partners, Florintree Infra and founder Swapnil Shah — for an aggregate ₹95.66 crore. TT&A advised Tata Motors; S&R Associates advised Freight Tiger and founder Swapnil Shah; SAM advised Lightspeed India Partners; Agram Legal Consultants advised Florintree Infra.

firms.name: Shardul Amarchand Mangaldas
firms.note: Acted for the selling shareholder Lightspeed; deal team per the announcement.

firms.name: Agram Legal Consultants
firms.note: Acted for the selling shareholder Florintree Infra.

sources.name: Bar & Bench — Dealstreet
sources.blurb: “Tata Motors Limited has increased its stake in Freight Commerce Solutions (Freight Tiger) to ~ 63%…for an aggregate amount of ₹95.66 crore.” — names all four advising firms and their respective sides.

sources.name: ScanX Market News
sources.blurb: Confirms the ~18% additional stake for ₹95.66 cr taking Tata Motors to ~63.6% on a fully diluted basis — Freight Tiger becomes a subsidiary.

sources.name: Legal Era

timeline.t: Tata Motors crosses ~63% in Freight Tiger
